decision_rule_fixed_here: SAME-FLIGHT NODE-TEMPLATE COLUMN READ (NX programme C0.2/C2 R1 iteration 2; instrument E1/E2; claim ceiling 'nominated'). One flight, one Solver visit per row, seven arms over the SAME QueryState and evidence: r1-i2-c1 .. r1-i2-c5 (hand-written candidates), aa (the twin, replicate_of lock) and lock (the locked template, delivering, last). NOMINATION IS DECIDED ON THE OFFICIAL COLUMN. Each arm's first-visit Solver answer is rendered through the delivered row's normaliser and projection and scored ONCE with slurp-slu-official-train (never sharded); every contrast is the paired ROW bootstrap of that arm's column against the delivering lock arm (cluster key sample_id, 10,000 draws, seed 20260915; scripts/analysis/stage3_rollout_score.py then stage3_paired_read.py), all read within this one flight. NOMINATION RULE: candidate X is NOMINATED iff (a) the official pooled SLU-F1 delta X minus lock has a CI95 lower bound > 0, AND (b) that delta is above the aa twin's official pooled SLU-F1 delta (aa minus lock, same flight), AND (c) the intent guard holds: rows whose official intent correctness differs from lock <= 7 (the floor 0.65 pp of 1,080). HARM iff the official pooled SLU-F1 delta CI95 upper bound < 0. The twin null (aa minus lock) is read first and reported beside the design's provisional floor (SLU-F1 1.49 pp, intent 0.65 pp at n = 1,080; borrowed from same-flight-supply-variant until this cell measures its own null). Among several NOMINATED arms the largest official SLU-F1 delta wins (ties: fewer words). THE NODE-LOCAL READ IS DIAGNOSTIC AND GATES NOTHING: the E2 reader (schema v2; scripts/analysis/slurp_nx_solver_column_read.py) reports exact_set_normalised (the entity exact-set per row of the answer after the delivered row's own normaliser), parse_valid, empty_gold_false_fill, nonempty_exact, per-slot-type counts and the raw-vs-normalised flip table, paired per row against lock, to localise where an official delta comes from; a node-local gain without an official gain is not a nomination, and a nomination needs no node-local screen. (Why: in iteration 1 the node-local screen and the official column disagreed: normalised node-local c5 +1.30 [-0.19, +2.78] vs official -0.15 [-1.23, +0.89]; c3 +4.63 [+2.87, +6.39] vs official +0.96 [-0.16, +2.09].) PLATEAU RULE (programme C0.4): two evaluated rounds without a NOMINATED arm lock the delivering template and close the node. A nomination is confirmed once on TRAIN Fold A as a two-arm column before any lock; it admits nothing by itself. The delivering lock arm's own offline post-processing columns v4 and v4g are read beside (analysis recipe, offline_columns). THIS IS THE SECOND AND LAST EVALUATED ROUND of R1 under the plateau rule: if no arm is NOMINATED here the delivering template is locked and the node closes. The iteration-1 arm r1-c5 does NOT fly in this column; each iteration-2 arm is also set beside iteration-1 r1-c5 in a cross-iteration table that is DESCRIPTIVE only (different flights, different offsets: no claim, no nomination, no input to the rule above). Iteration 1's registered rule and verdict stand as written.
development_numbers_only: Every number is a TRAIN Fold B development number (owner decisions 28 and 86), never a test claim.
failure_policy: Stop and preserve on the first failure. AT MOST ONE root-diagnosed recovery re-registration; a second failure closes the cell and the fix is proven on a four-row dry run. The budget is run-cumulative across attempts.
one_factor: the Solver instruction template (phase_material.solver.instruction_template) of each non-delivering arm: ONE hash-pinned path per arm under probes/nx/solver/r1/, nothing else (no supply knob, decoding, response format or tool authority); the base, the Fold B pins, the review-off program and the module block are the instrument's carrier, shared by every arm
prohibitions: No test-split, DEV or Fold A contact or read (Fold A confirms only a later two-arm column, under its own registration).
No second factor: one axis (the Solver instruction template), none on aa or lock.
No tool schema on any role; no Reviewer or Planner visit; max_revisions 0.
No v4 or v4g normaliser wired into the cell: the runtime delivery normaliser is the COMP-1b module cell's (v3); v4 and v4g are OFFLINE read columns only.
No flight before root countersigns the DRAFT rows, mints the decision receipt and the cells are flipped.
No arm score opened before the READ row is root countersigned.
No system-level claim: a column effect may only nominate.
the_question: At the one Solver visit of every TRAIN Fold B row of the review-off COMP-1b module graph, does any of five hand-written Solver instruction templates raise the OFFICIAL pooled SLU-F1 of the delivered column over the locked template (paired per row inside one flight, CI95 lower bound above zero), by more than the in-flight twin's delta, without an intent loss beyond the floor? (The node-local exact-set read is diagnostic.)
